sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sthite muhūrtaṃ pārthe tu dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire ājagmus tatra kauravya devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Pārtha, Yudhiṣṭhira the king of righteousness, had stood there a moment, O Kauravya, the gods came to that place, led by Śakra.

sanskrit: svayaṃ vigrahavān dharmo rājānaṃ prasamīkṣitum tatrājagāma yatrāsau kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Dharma himself, embodied in form, came there to behold the king, to the very spot where the Kuru lord Yudhiṣṭhira stood.

sanskrit: teṣu bhāsvaradeheṣu puṇyābhijanakarmasu samāgateṣu deveṣu vyagamat tat tamo nṛpa
english: When those gods of radiant bodies, of holy birth and holy deeds, had assembled, that darkness vanished, O king.

sanskrit: nādṛśyanta ca tās tatra yātanāḥ pāpakarmiṇām nadī vaitaraṇī caiva kūṭaśālmalinā saha
english: And there the torments of the evildoers were no longer to be seen, neither the river Vaitaraṇī nor the spiked silk-cotton tree.

sanskrit: lohakumbhyaḥ śilāś caiva nādṛśyanta bhayānakāḥ vikṛtāni śarīrāṇi yāni tatra samantataḥ dadarśa rājā kaunteyas tāny adṛśyāni cābhavan
english: The iron cauldrons and the dreadful rocks were seen no more; and those mangled bodies which the son of Kuntī had beheld everywhere about him—these too became invisible.

sanskrit: tato vāyuḥ sukhasparśaḥ puṇyagandhavahaḥ śivaḥ vavau devasamīpasthaḥ śītalo 'tīva bhārata
english: Then a wind, soft to the touch, bearing holy fragrances, auspicious and most cool, blew there near the gods, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: marutaḥ saha śakreṇa vasavaś cāśvinau saha sādhyā rudrās tathādityā ye cānye 'pi divaukasaḥ
english: The Maruts with Śakra, the Vasus together with the two Aśvins, the Sādhyas, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and whatever other dwellers of heaven there were—

sanskrit: sarve tatra samājagmuḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ yatra rājā mahātejā dharmaputraḥ sthito 'bhavat
english: all of them assembled there, together with the Siddhas and the supreme sages, where the king of great splendour, the son of Dharma, was standing.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraḥ surapatiḥ śriyā paramayā yutaḥ yudhiṣṭhiram uvācedaṃ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Śakra, lord of the gods, endowed with supreme majesty, spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira these soothing words:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho prītā devagaṇās tava ehy ehi puruṣavyāghra kṛtam etāvatā vibho siddhiḥ prāptā tvayā rājaṃl lokāś cāpy akṣayās tava
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira, mighty-armed one, the hosts of the gods are pleased with you. Come, come, O tiger among men; enough has been done, O lord. Perfection has been attained by you, O king, and yours are the imperishable worlds.

sanskrit: na ca manyus tvayā kāryaḥ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama avaśyaṃ narakas tāta draṣṭavyaḥ sarvarājabhiḥ
english: You should harbour no anger; and hear these words of mine. Hell must of necessity be seen, dear son, by every king.

sanskrit: śubhānām aśubhānāṃ ca dvau rāśī puruṣarṣabha yaḥ pūrvaṃ sukṛtaṃ bhuṅkte paścān nirayam eti saḥ pūrvaṃ narakabhāgyas tu paścāt svargam upaiti saḥ
english: There are two heaps, O bull among men, of good deeds and of evil. He who first enjoys the fruit of his good deeds goes afterward to hell; but he whose lot is hell first attains heaven afterward.

sanskrit: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ pāpakarmā yaḥ sa pūrvaṃ svargam aśnute tena tvam evaṃ gamito mayā śreyorthinā nṛpa
english: He whose deeds are mostly evil enjoys heaven first; and therefore, O king, I, seeking your good, led you there in this manner.

sanskrit: vyājena hi tvayā droṇa upacīrṇaḥ sutaṃ prati vyājenaiva tato rājan darśito narakas tava
english: For by a deception you deceived Droṇa concerning his son; and so by a deception, O king, hell was shown to you.

sanskrit: yathaiva tvaṃ tathā bhīmas tathā pārtho yamau tathā draupadī ca tathā kṛṣṇā vyājena narakaṃ gatāḥ
english: As you did, so did Bhīma, so Pārtha, so the twins, and so too Kṛṣṇā Draupadī—through deception they went to hell.

sanskrit: āgaccha naraśārdūla muktās te caiva kilbiṣāt svapakṣāś caiva ye tubhyaṃ pārthivā nihatā raṇe sarve svargam anuprāptās tān paśya puruṣarṣabha
english: Come, O tiger among men; they are freed from their sin. And those kings of your own side who were slain in battle for you have all attained heaven—behold them, O bull among men.

sanskrit: karṇaś caiva maheṣvāsaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ sa gataḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ yadarthaṃ paritapyase
english: And Karṇa, the great archer, the foremost of all who bear weapons—he for whose sake you grieve has gone to the supreme perfection.

sanskrit: taṃ paśya puruṣavyāghram ādityatanayaṃ vibho svasthānasthaṃ mahābāho jahi śokaṃ nararṣabha
english: Behold him, that tiger among men, the son of the Sun, O lord, established in his own station, mighty-armed one; cast off your grief, O bull among men.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṃś cānyāṃs tathā paśya svapakṣāṃś caiva pārthivān svaṃ svaṃ sthānam anuprāptān vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: Behold too your brothers and the other kings of your own side, each arrived at his own proper station; let the fever of your mind depart.

sanskrit: anubhūya pūrvaṃ tvaṃ kṛcchram itaḥ prabhṛti kaurava viharasva mayā sārdhaṃ gataśoko nirāmayaḥ
english: Having endured hardship before, from this point onward, O Kaurava, sport with me, free of grief and free of affliction.

sanskrit: karmaṇāṃ tāta puṇyānāṃ jitānāṃ tapasā svayam dānānāṃ ca mahābāho phalaṃ prāpnuhi pāṇḍava
english: Reap now, dear son, the fruit of your holy deeds, won by your own austerity, and of your gifts, O mighty-armed son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: adya tvāṃ devagandharvā divyāś cāpsaraso divi upasevantu kalyāṇaṃ virajombaravāsasaḥ
english: This day let the gods and Gandharvas and the celestial Apsarases, clad in spotless garments, attend upon you in your blessedness in heaven.

sanskrit: rājasūyajitāṃl lokān aśvamedhābhivardhitān prāpnuhi tvaṃ mahābāho tapasaś ca phalaṃ mahat
english: Attain, O mighty-armed one, the worlds won by your Rājasūya and increased by the Aśvamedha, and the great fruit of your austerity.

sanskrit: upary upari rājñāṃ hi tava lokā yudhiṣṭhira hariścandrasamāḥ pārtha yeṣu tvaṃ vihariṣyasi
english: Far above the worlds of other kings are your worlds, Yudhiṣṭhira—equal to those of Hariścandra, O Pārtha—in which you shall take your delight.

sanskrit: māndhātā yatra rājarṣir yatra rājā bhagīrathaḥ dauḥṣantir yatra bharatas tatra tvaṃ vihariṣyasi
english: Where the royal sage Māndhātṛ is, where King Bhagīratha is, where Bharata the son of Duḥṣanta is—there shall you take your delight.

sanskrit: eṣā devanadī puṇyā pārtha trailokyapāvanī ākāśagaṅgā rājendra tatrāplutya gamiṣyasi
english: This is the holy river of the gods, O Pārtha, that purifies the three worlds—the heavenly Gaṅgā, O lord of kings; bathing therein you shall go forward.

sanskrit: atra snātasya te bhāvo mānuṣo vigamiṣyati gataśoko nirāyāso muktavairo bhaviṣyasi
english: When you have bathed here your human nature will pass away; rid of grief and of toil, freed from enmity you shall become."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati devendre kauravendraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram dharmo vigrahavān sākṣād uvāca sutam ātmanaḥ
english: While the lord of the gods was thus speaking to Yudhiṣṭhira, lord of the Kurus, Dharma, visibly embodied in form, addressed his own son:

sanskrit: bho bho rājan mahāprājña prīto 'smi tava putraka madbhaktyā satyavākyena kṣamayā ca damena ca
english: "Ho, O king of great wisdom, I am pleased with you, my son, by your devotion to me, by your truthful speech, by your forbearance and your self-restraint.

sanskrit: eṣā tṛtīyā jijñāsā tava rājan kṛtā mayā na śakyase cālayituṃ svabhāvāt pārtha hetubhiḥ
english: This is the third test of you, O king, that I have made; you cannot be moved from your nature by any inducements, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ parīkṣito hi tvam āsīr dvaitavanaṃ prati araṇīsahitasyārthe tac ca nistīrṇavān asi
english: Earlier you were tested in the Dvaita forest, over the matter of the fire-drill and its kindling-stick, and you passed that trial.

sanskrit: sodaryeṣu vinaṣṭeṣu draupadyāṃ tatra bhārata śvarūpadhāriṇā putra punas tvaṃ me parīkṣitaḥ
english: When your own brothers had fallen, and Draupadī too, there, O Bhārata, you were tested by me again, my son, in the form of a dog.

sanskrit: idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bhrātṝṇām arthe yat sthātum icchasi viśuddho 'si mahābhāga sukhī vigatakalmaṣaḥ
english: This is the third—that you wished to remain here for your brothers' sake. You are wholly pure, O greatly fortunate one, happy and free from all stain.

sanskrit: na ca te bhrātaraḥ pārtha narakasthā viśāṃ pate māyaiṣā devarājena mahendreṇa prayojitā
english: And your brothers, O Pārtha, are not in hell, O lord of peoples; this was an illusion employed by the king of the gods, the great Indra.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ narakas tāta draṣṭavyaḥ sarvarājabhiḥ tatas tvayā prāptam idaṃ muhūrtaṃ duḥkham uttamam
english: Hell must of necessity be seen, dear son, by all kings; and so for this brief moment you received this extreme of suffering.

sanskrit: na savyasācī bhīmo vā yamau vā puruṣarṣabhau karṇo vā satyavāk śūro narakārhāś ciraṃ nṛpa
english: Neither Savyasācin nor Bhīma, nor the twins, those bulls among men, nor the truthful, heroic Karṇa deserve to remain long in hell, O king.

sanskrit: na kṛṣṇā rājaputrī ca narakārhā yudhiṣṭhira ehy ehi bharataśreṣṭha paśya gaṅgāṃ trilokagām
english: Nor does the princess Kṛṣṇā deserve hell, Yudhiṣṭhira. Come, come, O best of the Bharatas; behold the Gaṅgā that flows through the three worlds."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājarṣis tava pūrvapitāmahaḥ jagāma saha dharmeṇa sarvaiś ca tridaśālayaiḥ
english: Thus addressed, that royal sage, your forefather of old, went on together with Dharma and with all the dwellers of the threefold heaven.

sanskrit: gaṅgāṃ devanadīṃ puṇyāṃ pāvanīm ṛṣisaṃstutām avagāhya tu tāṃ rājā tanuṃ tatyāja mānuṣīm
english: And having plunged into the Gaṅgā, the holy river of the gods, the purifier praised by the sages, the king cast off his human body.

sanskrit: tato divyavapur bhūtvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nirvairo gatasaṃtāpo jale tasmin samāplutaḥ
english: Then, becoming of celestial form, Yudhiṣṭhira the king of righteousness, free of enmity and free of sorrow, was bathed in that water.

sanskrit: tato yayau vṛto devaiḥ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dharmeṇa sahito dhīmān stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: Then the wise Yudhiṣṭhira, king of the Kurus, surrounded by the gods and accompanied by Dharma, went on, being praised by the great sages.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā devaiḥ sarṣimarudgaṇaiḥ pūjyamāno yayau tatra yatra te kurupuṃgavāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, honoured by the gods together with the hosts of sages and Maruts, went on to where those bulls of the Kurus were.

sanskrit: dadarśa tatra govindaṃ brāhmeṇa vapuṣānvitam tenaiva dṛṣṭapūrveṇa sādṛśyenopasūcitam
english: There he beheld Govinda invested with a brahmic form, recognizable by that very likeness he had seen before.

sanskrit: dīpyamānaṃ svavapuṣā divyair astrair upasthitam cakraprabhṛtibhir ghorair divyaiḥ puruṣavigrahaiḥ upāsyamānaṃ vīreṇa phalgunena suvarcasā
english: Blazing with his own splendour, attended by celestial weapons—the dread divine ones, the discus and the rest, in human form—and waited upon by the hero Phalguna of fair radiance.

sanskrit: aparasminn athoddeśe karṇaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam dvādaśādityasahitaṃ dadarśa kurunandanaḥ
english: Then in another place the joy of the Kurus beheld Karṇa, the foremost of weapon-bearers, in the company of the twelve Ādityas.

sanskrit: athāparasminn uddeśe marudgaṇavṛtaṃ prabhum bhīmasenam athāpaśyat tenaiva vapuṣānvitam
english: And in yet another place he saw the lordly Bhīmasena, surrounded by the host of the Maruts, invested with that very form.

sanskrit: aśvinos tu tathā sthāne dīpyamānau svatejasā nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca dadarśa kurunandanaḥ
english: And in the station of the two Aśvins the joy of the Kurus beheld Nakula and Sahadeva, blazing with their own splendour.

sanskrit: tathā dadarśa pāñcālīṃ kamalotpalamālinīm vapuṣā svargam ākramya tiṣṭhantīm arkavarcasam
english: And so he beheld the Pāñcāla princess, garlanded with lotuses and blue lilies, standing with her form filling heaven, radiant as the sun.

sanskrit: athaināṃ sahasā rājā praṣṭum aicchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tato 'sya bhagavān indraḥ kathayām āsa devarāṭ
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira at once wished to question her; whereupon the lord Indra, king of the gods, told him:

sanskrit: śrīr eṣā draupadīrūpā tvadarthe mānuṣaṃ gatā ayonijā lokakāntā puṇyagandhā yudhiṣṭhira
english: "This is Śrī, in the form of Draupadī, who came into the mortal world for your sake—born of no womb, beloved of the worlds, of holy fragrance, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: drupadasya kule jātā bhavadbhiś copajīvitā ratyarthaṃ bhavatāṃ hy eṣā nirmitā śūlapāṇinā
english: Born in the line of Drupada, and shared as your wife, she was fashioned by the trident-bearer for your delight.

sanskrit: ete pañca mahābhāgā gandharvāḥ pāvakaprabhāḥ draupadyās tanayā rājan yuṣmākam amitaujasaḥ
english: These five greatly fortunate ones, Gandharvas radiant as fire, are the sons of Draupadī, O king—yours, of measureless might.

sanskrit: paśya gandharvarājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam enaṃ ca tvaṃ vijānīhi bhrātaraṃ pūrvajaṃ pituḥ
english: Behold the king of the Gandharvas, the sagacious Dhṛtarāṣṭra; and know him to be the elder brother of your father.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te pūrvajo bhrātā kaunteyaḥ pāvakadyutiḥ sūryaputro 'grajaḥ śreṣṭho rādheya iti viśrutaḥ ādityasahito yāti paśyainaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: This is your elder brother, the son of Kuntī, of fire-like brilliance, the son of the Sun, your firstborn and foremost, renowned as Rādheya; he goes in the company of the Ādityas—behold him, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sādhyānām atha devānāṃ vasūnāṃ marutām api gaṇeṣu paśya rājendra vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathān sātyakipramukhān vīrān bhojāṃś caiva mahārathān
english: Among the hosts of the Sādhyas, the gods, the Vasus, and the Maruts, behold, O lord of kings, the great chariot-warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, the heroes led by Sātyaki, and the Bhojas, the mighty car-warriors.

sanskrit: somena sahitaṃ paśya saubhadram aparājitam abhimanyuṃ maheṣvāsaṃ niśākarasamadyutim
english: Behold, in the company of Soma, the unconquered son of Subhadrā—Abhimanyu, the great archer, of splendour like the moon.

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍur maheṣvāsaḥ kuntyā mādryā ca saṃgataḥ vimānena sadābhyeti pitā tava mamāntikam
english: This is Pāṇḍu, the great archer, reunited with Kuntī and Mādrī; your father comes ever to my presence by his celestial car.

sanskrit: vasubhiḥ sahitaṃ paśya bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ nṛpam droṇaṃ bṛhaspateḥ pārśve gurum enaṃ niśāmaya
english: Behold King Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, in the company of the Vasus; and mark this Droṇa, your teacher, at the side of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: ete cānye mahīpālā yodhās tava ca pāṇḍava gandharvaiḥ sahitā yānti yakṣaiḥ puṇyajanais tathā
english: These and other lords of the earth, and your warriors too, O son of Pāṇḍu, go in the company of the Gandharvas and the Yakṣas, those holy beings.

sanskrit: guhyakānāṃ gatiṃ cāpi ke cit prāptā nṛsattamāḥ tyaktvā dehaṃ jitasvargāḥ puṇyavāgbuddhikarmabhiḥ
english: And some of those best of men have attained the state of the Guhyakas, having cast off the body and won heaven by holy speech, thought, and deeds."

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bhīṣmadroṇau mahātmānau dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca pārthivaḥ virāṭadrupadau cobhau śaṅkhaś caivottaras tathā
english: Janamejaya said: The high-souled Bhīṣma and Droṇa, and King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and both Virāṭa and Drupada, and Śaṅkha and Uttara as well,

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketur jayatseno rājā caiva sa satyajit duryodhanasutāś caiva śakuniś caiva saubalaḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭaketu, Jayatsena, and King Satyajit, and the sons of Duryodhana, and Śakuni the son of Subala,

sanskrit: karṇaputrāś ca vikrāntā rājā caiva jayadrathaḥ ghaṭotkacādayaś caiva ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ
english: and the valiant sons of Karṇa, and King Jayadratha, and Ghaṭotkaca and the rest, and the others not here named—

sanskrit: ye cānye kīrtitās tatra rājāno dīptamūrtayaḥ svarge kālaṃ kiyantaṃ te tasthus tad api śaṃsa me
english: and those other kings of radiant form who were named there—for how long a time did they abide in heaven? Tell me that as well.

sanskrit: āho svic chāśvataṃ sthānaṃ teṣāṃ tatra dvijottama ante vā karmaṇaḥ kāṃ te gatiṃ prāptā nararṣabhāḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ procyamānaṃ tvayā dvija
english: Or is their station there eternal, O best of the twice-born? Or at the end of their deeds, what destiny did those bulls among men attain? This I wish to hear, told by you, O brahmin.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tu viprarṣir anujñāto mahātmanā vyāsena tasya nṛpater ākhyātum upacakrame
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed, that sage among brahmins, given leave by the high-souled Vyāsa, began to recount it to that king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gantavyaṃ karmaṇām ante sarveṇa manujādhipa śṛṇu guhyam idaṃ rājan devānāṃ bharatarṣabha yad uvāca mahātejā divyacakṣuḥ pratāpavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At the end of his deeds everyone must depart, O lord of men. Hear this secret of the gods, O king, O bull of the Bharatas, which the one of great splendour, of divine sight, the mighty—

sanskrit: muniḥ purāṇaḥ kauravya pārāśaryo mahāvrataḥ agādhabuddhiḥ sarvajño gatijñaḥ sarvakarmaṇām
english: the ancient sage, O Kauravya, the son of Parāśara of great vows, of fathomless intellect, omniscient, knowing the destinies of all deeds—declared.

sanskrit: vasūn eva mahātejā bhīṣmaḥ prāpa mahādyutiḥ aṣṭāv eva hi dṛśyante vasavo bharatarṣabha
english: Bhīṣma of great splendour and great brilliance attained the Vasus themselves; for indeed only eight Vasus are now seen, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiṃ viveśātha droṇo hy aṅgirasāṃ varam kṛtavarmā tu hārdikyaḥ praviveśa marudgaṇam
english: Then Droṇa entered into Bṛhaspati, the best of the line of Aṅgiras; and Kṛtavarman the son of Hṛdika entered the host of the Maruts.

sanskrit: sanatkumāraṃ pradyumnaḥ praviveśa yathāgatam dhṛtarāṣṭro dhaneśasya lokān prāpa durāsadān
english: Pradyumna entered into Sanatkumāra, whence he had come; and Dhṛtarāṣṭra attained the worlds of the lord of wealth, hard to reach.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa sahitā gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī patnībhyāṃ sahitaḥ pāṇḍur mahendrasadanaṃ yayau
english: And the illustrious Gāndhārī went together with Dhṛtarāṣṭra; and Pāṇḍu, together with his two wives, went to the abode of the great Indra.

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau cobhau dhṛṣṭaketuś ca pārthivaḥ niśaṭhākrūrasāmbāś ca bhānuḥ kampo viḍūrathaḥ
english: Both Virāṭa and Drupada, and King Dhṛṣṭaketu, and Niśaṭha, Akrūra, and Sāmba, and Bhānu, Kampa, and Viḍūratha,

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaś caiva bhūriś ca pṛthivīpatiḥ ugrasenas tathā kaṃso vasudevaś ca vīryavān
english: Bhūriśravas and Śala, and Bhūri the lord of the earth, and Ugrasena, and Kaṃsa, and the valiant Vāsudeva,

sanskrit: uttaraś ca saha bhrātrā śaṅkhena narapuṃgavaḥ viśveṣāṃ devatānāṃ te viviśur narasattamāḥ
english: and Uttara, that bull among men, together with his brother Śaṅkha—these best of men entered into the All-Gods, the Viśvedevas.

sanskrit: varcā nāma mahātejāḥ somaputraḥ pratāpavān so 'bhimanyur nṛsiṃhasya phalgunasya suto 'bhavat
english: The son of Soma, named Varcas, of great splendour and might, became Abhimanyu, the son of Phalguna, that lion among men.

sanskrit: sa yuddhvā kṣatradharmeṇa yathā nānyaḥ pumān kva cit viveśa somaṃ dharmātmā karmaṇo 'nte mahārathaḥ
english: Having fought by the law of the warrior as no other man anywhere had done, that righteous great car-warrior, at the end of his deeds, entered into Soma.

sanskrit: āviveśa raviṃ karṇaḥ pitaraṃ puruṣarṣabha dvāparaṃ śakuniḥ prāpa dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu pāvakam
english: Karṇa entered the Sun, his father, O bull among men; Śakuni attained Dvāpara, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the fire-god.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajāḥ sarve yātudhānā balotkaṭāḥ ṛddhimanto mahātmānaḥ śastrapūtā divaṃ gatāḥ dharmam evāviśat kṣattā rājā caiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: All the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, fierce in might, were Rākṣasas; prosperous and high-souled, purified by the weapon, they went to heaven. And the Kṣattṛ (Vidura) entered into Dharma himself, as did King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ananto bhagavān devaḥ praviveśa rasātalam pitāmahaniyogād dhi yo yogād gām adhārayat
english: The blessed god Ananta entered the nether region, Rasātala—he who, by the command of the Grandsire, by his yoga upheld the earth.
